name: email-quoted-localpart-smuggle-at-bypass-invalid
description: excludedSubtrees rfc822Name is host-form 'example.com' (no '@', so the constraint matches any mailbox whose host part equals example.com or any subdomain). The leaf SAN encodes a quoted-string local-part that itself contains an '@' character: '"a@b"@example.com'. Per RFC 5321 §4.1.2 and RFC 5322 §3.4.1 the mailbox is parsed by splitting at the *unquoted* '@' that separates the local-part from the domain — the quoted-string's contents (including its embedded '@') are part of the local-part, and the domain part is unambiguously 'example.com'. A conforming validator therefore sees host=example.com, fires the exclusion, and rejects the chain. A validator that splits the mailbox on the first '@' (a common shortcut) sees host='b"@example.com', which is not exactly 'example.com' and not a subdomain of it, so the exclusion does not fire and the chain is incorrectly accepted.
notes: Constructed via unknown_extensions because cryptography.x509.RFC822Name does not preserve a leading double quote in the local-part.

Bug bait: first-'@' splitting was the root of multiple historical email-comparison CVEs. The quoted-localpart form is rare but legal, and an attacker who can place this mailbox in a SAN can route past naive host-form exclusion lists.

Companion to `email-quoted-localpart-not-equal-invalid`, which probes the quoted-vs-unquoted local-part comparison rule when both sides agree on the host. Here the host is the comparison target and the quoted form is the attack vector.
